Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Newly diagnosed breast cancer patients ≤65 years old
Required findings: Personal history of breast cancer (stage I‑III or de novo stage IV/metastatic) diagnosed at age 65 or younger
No requirement for additional risk factors; testing should include BRCA1, BRCA2 (and PALB2 as appropriate)
Documentation of diagnosis, stage, and pathology (ER/PR/HER2 status) to support treatment impact
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > BRCA Analysis > Guidelines and evidence

Required findings: Age at diagnosis greater than 65 years

At least one of the following: candidate for PARP‑inhibitor therapy, triple‑negative breast cancer, personal or family history suggestive of a pathogenic variant, male sex at birth, Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry or other population with known founder mutations
Relevant tumor pathology (e.g., triple‑negative status) and treatment plan indicating potential PARP‑inhibitor use
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > BRCA Analysis > Guidelines and evidence

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Patients with a second primary breast cancer (contralateral or ipsilateral)
Required findings: Documented second primary invasive breast cancer in the contralateral or ipsilateral breast
Prior breast cancer history confirmed by pathology reports
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > BRCA Analysis > Guidelines and evidence

Required findings: Confirmed diagnosis of epithelial ovarian cancer (any stage)
Recommendation per ASCO 2025 to perform germline (and somatic) BRCA1/BRCA2 testing
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > BRCA Analysis > Guidelines and evidence

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Patients with metastatic prostate cancer (hormone‑sensitive or castration‑resistant)
Required findings: Diagnosis of metastatic hormone‑sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) or metastatic castration‑resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC)
Clinical indication for germline testing to guide PARP‑inhibitor eligibility or other targeted therapy
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > BRCA Analysis > Guidelines and evidence

Required findings: No personal history of cancer but a family history that meets NCCN thresholds (e.g., first‑degree relative with breast, ovarian, pancreatic, or prostate cancer; known pathogenic BRCA variant in family; Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry)
Completion of a brief familial risk assessment tool with a positive result
Genetic counseling documentation confirming discussion of limited value of testing unaffected relatives when an affected relative is unavailable
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > BRCA Analysis > Guidelines and evidence

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Patients with prior negative germline BRCA1/2 testing performed before 2014
Required findings: History of prior germline BRCA1/2 testing performed before 2014 (likely lacking PALB2 and large‑genomic‑rearrangement analysis)
Current clinical scenario (personal or family history) that raises suspicion for a pathogenic variant
Recommendation for updated multigene panel testing
Medical necessity indications.Source: Test Specific Guidelines > BRCA Analysis > Guidelines and evidence

Non-Indications: Women (or other individuals) whose personal and family history is not consistent with a BRCA1/2 mutation and who do not meet any NCCN risk criteria (USPSTF D‑grade recommendation against testing)
Patients >65 years old with breast cancer who lack all listed risk factors (no PARP‑inhibitor candidacy, not triple‑negative, no relevant family history, not male, no Ashkenazi or founder ancestry)
Universal testing of all breast cancer patients without consideration of age, tumor characteristics, or family history (per ACMG statement of insufficient evidence)
Individuals with a known pathogenic variant already documented and no change in clinical scenario that would alter management
Important criteria & exceptions: Age cutoff of 65 years for universal BRCA testing in newly diagnosed breast cancer; older patients require additional risk factors
Testing must include BRCA1 and BRAN2 (and PALB2 when indicated) and may be part of a multigene panel
Genetic counseling (by a certified genetic counselor or qualified provider) is required before testing
Updated testing is recommended for patients with prior negative results performed before 2014 due to expanded gene coverage
Cascade testing is recommended for at‑risk family members when a pathogenic variant is identified
Risk assessment tools (e.g., brief familial risk assessment) must be completed for unaffected individuals before testing
Documentation required: Physician order specifying the indication for BRCA testing
Comprehensive personal cancer history (diagnosis date, stage, pathology, receptor status for breast cancer; histology for ovarian or prostate cancer)
Detailed three‑generation family cancer history, including type of cancer, age at diagnosis, and relationship
Pathology reports confirming tumor characteristics (e.g., triple‑negative status, grade, histology)
Prior genetic test reports (if any), especially for tests performed before 2014
Ancestry documentation when Ashkenazi Jewish or other founder population is claimed
Result of a validated familial risk assessment tool (for unaffected individuals)
Genetic counseling note documenting pre‑test counseling, discussion of risks/benefits, and patient consent
